target: midrib of the fertile scale (glume/floral scale, PO_0009039 region), not leaf midvein
fix: A 'midrib' that follows a scale description belongs to that scale (here the fertile spikelet scale), not to the leaf. Bind 'midrib' to the nearest preceding organ in the same clause chain.
reason: The statement is about the midrib of the fertile scales of the spikelet ('fertile scales ... keeled ... midrib included or excurrent as mucro'), not a leaf midvein. The values are right.

fix: Map 'tepals' to tepal PO_0009033, not petal. Iridaceae have tepals.
reason: The flora says tepals. PO has tepal (PO_0009033). The colour values are right; 'bases yellow' is a separate statement.

fix: In a head, 'golden yellow disk florets' is about the disk flowers (PO_0025332). Also, 'golden' is a shade word, not an approximation, so it should not set value_qualifier 'approximately'.
reason: Golden yellow is said of the disk florets. The ray florets are described separately (yellow). The approximate qualifier is also spurious.
'Shrubs' gives the shrub (frutescent) habit of the whole plant. 'Deciduous' is a separate quality and is not misrepresented here.

target: stem height relative to whole plant (PO_0000003), ratio up to 0.2
fix: 'N/M height of X' is a relative measure: a 'towards' slot with the target part and ratio N/M. It is not an absolute length, and no unit should be converted.
reason: The flora gives a fraction of the plant height (up to 1/5), not 2 cm. The absolute value was computed or misparsed from '1/ 5' and the dm of the plant size.

11–16 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The count and the each-side position with the midvein landmark are right. 'Vascular bundle' is a broad but acceptable bearer, since PO has no secondary-vein class. The leaf is a leaflet blade, but the statement still holds.
Caudate describes a tail-like apex, so 'leaf caudate' says what 'apex caudate-acuminate' says for the stem leaf. Naming leaf apex PO_0020137 would be more precise but is not needed for truth.
Flowers whitish to pale yellow: a colour continuum from white (FLOPO_0988009) to pale yellow (FLOPO_0988113), with 'whitish' giving the approximate qualifier.

fix: Map 'tepals: outer ...' to tepal PO_0009033 with the outer position (rule C374), not petal.
reason: The flora describes the outer tepals of Erythronium as ± white tinged pink. The bearer petal is wrong, and the outer position is dropped.
The culms (stems) are described as smooth.
Fruits straight or curved: the alternatives are right. The direction 'inward' is lost, but the statement stays true.
The leaf blade base is decurrent. Substituting the base as bearer is right.
The lamina is 3-lobed, so the count of lamina lobes is 3.
The stipules are glabrous or hairy. Bearer and alternatives match.
Capitula numerous: the inflorescences are present in many. True, though the bearer could be the more specific capitulum.

target: obtuse (PATO_0001935) / rounded apex shape, on petal apex (PO_0025144)
fix: A plain 'rounded' describing an apex is an absolute shape, not the comparative 'more rounded' (FLOPO_0980236). Map it as for 'rounded' elsewhere (obtuse/rounded) and use the apex as bearer.
reason: The flora says the petal apex is rounded or obtuse. 'More rounded' is a comparative quality that the source does not state.
3–8 bracteoles in the umbellet.
2–4 flowers at each node of the inflorescence. The count and the per-node position are right.

fix: A parenthetical '(not spiny)' after 'margins coarsely toothed' negates spininess of the margin teeth. Bind it to the margin, not to the blade.
reason: 'Not spiny' qualifies the toothed margins, not the blade as a whole.

target: cell wall (GO_0005618) of leaf cell, increased thickness
fix: In bryophyte descriptions, 'incrassate' cells means thick-walled cells: the thickness inheres in the cell wall, not the cell.
reason: Incrassate upper leaf cells have thickened walls. The cell itself is not 'thick'. The container (leaf) is right.
Leaf blade 4–12 × 2–5 cm: the width is 2–5 cm.
The petals are described as rounded (at the apex). Mapping this to obtuse follows the usual reading.

target: position: upper sterile part of the male zone of the spadix
fix: Measurements of a named zone of a part ('upper part of the male zone ... 1.7–2.2 cm diameter') need the region/position slot or a zone bearer, not the whole organ.
reason: The diameter is of the upper sterile male zone, not of the whole spadix.
Corolle infundibuliforme = funnel-shaped corolla.
The petiole is subrhombic in cross section: rhomboid with the approximate qualifier ('sub-'). The cross-section reading is implicit for a 2-D shape of an axis.
The peduncles are not dimorphic. The negation is right.
The pedicels elongate to 2.5 cm in fruit: length up to 2.5 cm at the fruiting stage.
The leaves are not constricted between sheath and blade. The negation is right. The position is implicit in 'leaf constricted'.
The capsule about equals the sepals in length: ratio 1, approximate.

fix: 'X at the base' after a leaf description describes the leaf base. Substitute the base as bearer (as in the place-on-the-part pattern).
reason: Rounded or slightly cuneate is said of the leaf base. A whole leaf that is cuneate or obtuse is a different statement.
